newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Telecom expected to seek US$860 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: China Telecom expected to seek US$860 mln loan.

text.p: China Telecom (Hong Kong) Ltd is expected to opt for a club deal to help fund its HK$9.177 billion investment in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, banking sources said on Monday.
About 20 banks are invited to lend a total of US$860 million between them in a one-year loan which is renewable for one year at China Telecom's request, the sources said.
They said the borrowing would be through a special-purpose company and is expected to pay a margin of about 20 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
Front-end fees are 15 basis points for an all-in return of 35 basis points. If renewed, an extension fee would be paid.
Bankers said China Telecom would pledge its Hongkong Telecom shares as security and that its parent would also issue a letter of comfort.
The company is indirectly held by China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, the nation's dominant telecoms provider.
Earlier this month, China Telecom agreed to pay Cable & Wireless Plc HK$14.25 a share or HK$9.177 billion for 5.5 percent of Hongkong Telecom.
It was the second investment by a mainland entity in the utility in a month, and also the second such investment to be funded by a loan.
A unit of China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd said in May it was paying CITIC Pacific Ltd HK$12.60 a share or a total of HK$11.4 billion for 7.74 percent of Hongkong Telecom.
Earlier this month, the China Everbright unit signed a US$1.05 billion loan to partly fund the investment.
China Everbright is one of 16 equal shareholders in China United Telecommunications Corp (China Unicom), the second largest telecom provider in China.
